Rules:
- Propose at most 3 things, the most valuable first. Cite the ids of the facts each one relies on.
- Use numbers exactly as they appear in the facts you cite (rounding is fine). Never compute new numbers.
- narrow_segment (keep only attribute=value) or exclude_segment (remove attribute=value) only when the cited segment fact says 'clearly different' for the chosen campaign type, and in the direction it shows. A segment that is 'not clearly different' is a reason NOT to narrow.
- switch_channel only if the cited channel fact says the other channel is allowed and the goal supports it.
- choose_campaign_type if the goal fits another type whose past results are clearly better, citing both.
- advice for a point to consider with no change (for example heavy recent contact). If nothing in the facts supports a change, return one advice titled 'Keep the audience as it is' and say why.

proposal.summary: The audience reaches 16,785 lines on SMS, with no contact pressure, but past app adoption campaigns show only a small uplift (+0.19 points, 95% -0.01 to +0.39). Email is not allowed for this audience under policy MKT-12, and no segment is clearly different.

proposals.title: Keep SMS as the only channel
proposals.rationale: Email is blocked for app-derived audiences by policy MKT-12, so SMS is the only usable channel. 6,667 lines without SMS consent are already left out, leaving 16,785 reachable lines.

proposals.title: Do not narrow by region, plan tier or device
proposals.rationale: No segment is clearly different for app adoption campaigns. The ios result (+0.47 points) is flagged as not clearly different, so narrowing to ios is not supported. Contact pressure is zero, so there is no reason to exclude anyone for fatigue.

proposals.title: Expect a modest uplift from this campaign type
proposals.rationale: Past app adoption campaigns gave +0.19 points against holdout, with the interval touching zero. Other types such as top-up reminders (+1.63) and data upsell (+0.93) did better, but they do not fit a newsletter about new plans, so no type change is proposed.
